knownGaps: Historical retrospective coverage (archiveDate-tagged entries) is CONTINUOUS across all 18 months from July 2024 through December 2025, AND continuous across all 7 elapsed 2026 months (01 through 07) as of this note. 2026-08 (the current month) is intentionally left for live/current coverage, not retrospective backfill. Remaining 2026 scope is simply: keep pace with the rest of the year as it happens, per WEEKLY_EDITORIAL_PROMPT.md's historical-backfill steps.

The 2026-01 entry originally risked a factual error: a secondary trade-media summary (Waste Dive) implied New York's commercial-organics-diversion threshold change took effect 1 January 2026, but the primary source (NY DEC's own landfill guidance PDF) confirms that specific change does not take effect until 1 January 2027. The published entry uses only the verified 25 December 2025 GHG-reporting law for New York and flags the organics-threshold date correctly in whatWeAreWatching. Treat this as a working example of why a secondary-source date claim always needs primary-source confirmation before publishing, not just a note about that one entry.

The 2025-12 energy-storage entry uses only ACP/Wood Mackenzie's figures (18.9 GW, 52%); a competing SEIA/Benchmark Mineral Intelligence report gave different figures (57.6 GWh, 30%) for what may be a different scope. Do not blend the two reports' numbers in a future piece without resolving why they diverge.

A prior version of this file and CLAUDE.md incorrectly claimed 'all of July-December 2024' was covered before August 2024 actually had an entry, that was a real documentation error, now corrected. Always verify claimed coverage against an actual query of lib/fieldNotes.ts (e.g. archiveDate distinct values), don't just trust the running narrative.
